counterfactual_missing_items: violaceous or polygonal papules and Wickham striae are absent
epidermal atrophy and orthokeratosis replace the usual acanthosis/hypergranulosis of lichen planus
papillary dermal homogenized collagen is unexplained by classic lichen planus
response.rationale: R1 is the only candidate supported by the lichenoid combination of flat-topped papules, pruritus, and bandlike lymphocytic infiltration. R2 and R3 only capture follicular keratotic features such as folliculocentric papules and keratin plugs, while ignoring the dermal homogenization, edema, eosinophils, and bandlike infiltrate; R4 lacks any nutritional context. Although R1 does not fully explain the sclerotic dermal change, it is the closest supplied diagnosis.

rejected.why: Matches follicular keratotic papules and keratin plugs but lacks the flat-topped morphology, pruritic inflammatory context, and bandlike lymphocytic infiltrate that are decisive.
Shares only nonspecific follicular keratosis features; typical extensor distribution, childhood onset, and family history are absent, and it does not explain the lichenoid/sclerotic histopathology.
No evidence of nutritional deficiency; follicular hyperkeratosis alone cannot account for the bandlike infiltrate, homogenized collagen, eosinophils, or steroid-responsive pruritic course.
